categories.main_business_segments: Ebara Jitsugyo operates three main business segments: Manufacturer Business (developing and selling environmental equipment such as ozone monitors, deodorization systems, water treatment plants, and ZEB/ZEH-related products), Engineering Business (design and construction of water treatment and other plant facilities, mainly for public sector clients), and Trading Business (procurement and sales of wind, hydraulic, and refrigeration equipment, including installation and related engineering services).
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary technologies in ozone measurement and application, deodorization, energy-saving blowers, water treatment, and ZEB/ZEH solutions. Manufacturing is fabless, with product development and design managed in-house and production outsourced to partner companies. R&D focuses on environmental measurement, energy-saving, deodorization, water treatment, and medical applications, often in collaboration with universities and external research institutions.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include Japanese government agencies and municipalities (public sector), which account for over 60% of sales, as well as private sector clients such as factories, commercial facilities, and the food retail industry. Major end markets are water infrastructure, environmental improvement, disaster prevention, energy management, and industrial facilities.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are primarily domestic, with sales and assets almost entirely in Japan. There is no significant overseas business, and international sales account for less than 10% of total revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: Ebara Jitsugyo operates mainly in the midstream and downstream of the supply chain, acting as a systems integrator, engineering contractor, and value-added distributor. It does not own manufacturing plants but manages product development and outsources production, while also procuring and integrating equipment from suppliers such as Ebara Corporation.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening existing businesses, exploring new domains, and enhancing management foundations. R&D is focused on environmental solutions such as decarbonization, water and air quality, energy efficiency, and disaster prevention. The company is investing in new product development, sustainability (including GHG reduction), and digital transformation, with a cumulative R&D investment target of 2.5 billion yen over the next mid-term plan.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through product sales (environmental equipment, measurement devices, ZEB/ZEH solutions), engineering and construction contracts (mainly for public infrastructure), and trading activities (procurement and resale of equipment). The company also earns income from maintenance services and, to a lesser extent, property leasing.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese engineering and environmental solution providers such as Ebara Corporation (with which it has a close business relationship), as well as firms specializing in water treatment, environmental equipment, and plant engineering. Ebara Jitsugyo positions itself as a leading total environmental solutions company with a strong public sector presence and a focus on integrated, value-added offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2024, consolidated net sales were 37.5 billion yen, with operating profit of 4.25 billion yen and net profit of 3.16 billion yen. The company has shown steady growth, with a 3.4% year-on-year increase in sales and a mid-term target of 45 billion yen in sales and 5.5 billion yen in operating profit by FY2027. The long-term vision aims for 60 billion yen in sales and 8 billion yen in operating profit by 2030.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Ebara Jitsugyo differentiates itself through its ability to provide comprehensive, integrated environmental solutions tailored to both public and private sector needs. Its strengths include proprietary technologies in ozone and deodorization, expertise in water and energy management, and a fabless, flexible production model that enables rapid innovation and customization. The company emphasizes sustainability, reliability, and the ability to address complex environmental and societal challenges.
